mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month predicts weakening consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes Fed tightening and higher inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% month-over-month, in the absence of a concurrent decline in unemployment, signals supply-side disruption and inflationary pressure, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate policy easing.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change < -1% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE not falling
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the Consumer Price Index above 4.5%, not accompanied by a concurrent increase in the federal funds rate, signals unanticipated inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL m/m change > 4.5% AND FEDFUNDS m/m change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 for four consecutive months, regardless of unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion and supports higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 m/m change < -1% AND HOUST m/m change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate, signals improving supply capacity and economic momentum, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change > 0.5% for three consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (|change| < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically above zero at 95% confidence.
